title: Countable categoricity: types, formulas and symmetry
summary: Characterize a unique countable model by finitely many tuple types, formula classes and automorphism orbits, and deduce finiteness of closures of finite sets.
abstract: In the rational order, any increasing pair can be moved to any other increasing pair by an order-preserving symmetry of the whole structure. Equal pairs and decreasing pairs give the other two possibilities. Why should a finite list of possibilities for every tuple length force a theory to have just one countable model? We prove that uniqueness is equivalent to having finitely many complete types, and to having finitely many formulas up to agreement throughout the theory, in each finite variable context. In the unique countable model, types are exactly the automorphism orbits. The same finiteness also limits what finitely many parameters can define: their algebraic closure is finite, and the substructure they generate has a bound depending only on the number of generators.
